Specification: This module specifies and proves properties of a voting protocol related to consensus, using acceptors, ballots, and quorums. It models acceptors maintaining a set of votes and a maximum ballot seen, defines a recursive safety predicate SafeAt, and proves state invariants ensuring vote consistency and safety. The file also contains TLAPS proofs showing inductive invariance, uniqueness of chosen values, refinement toward an instantiated Consensus specification, and a liveness assumption requiring weak fairness for some ballot actions while ruling out higher-ballot actions forever.

DivisionNotes: Partition count: StatePredicate(12) + TemporalProperty(3) + Init(1) + ValueDef(4) + ActionDefNames(5) = OperatorDefNames(25). Verified.

VT0 and VT1 are top-level operator definitions whose bodies are implication-valued state predicates over the current state; they contain no primes and no temporal operators, so they are placed in StatePredicate rather than TemporalProperty.

LiveAssumption is placed in TemporalProperty because it contains WF_vars(...) and [] [\A c \in Ballot : (c > b) => ~ BallotAction(self, c)]_vars; LiveSpec is temporal because it conjoins Spec with LiveAssumption.

TemporalNesting is false. The line `       /\ [] [\A c \in Ballot : (c > b) => ~ BallotAction(self, c)]_vars` contains [] applied to a temporal-subscript action formula, but no temporal operator is explicitly nested inside another temporal operator in the source text.
chosen is placed in ValueDef by elimination: it is a set-valued derived expression, not an action, init predicate, or temporal property.
UnchangedExprs_VarRef is empty because the only UNCHANGED occurrence is `UNCHANGED votes`, which is an explicit variable name rather than a previously defined tuple variable such as vars.
